feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: To get your next job — leave your iced coffee behind
entry.summary: One recruiter posted a TikTok advising potential job candidates to stop bringing iced coffees to interviews, and it sparked a massive internet debate.

entry.title: A surprising number of Americans use AI for spiritual reasons. Here's what they told us
entry.summary: While most people who use artificial intelligence do so for productivity help, a small but devoted group is turning to AI for religious and spiritual reasons.

entry.title: The Supreme Court revives a controversial data system for citizenship checks
entry.summary: The Supreme Court is allowing use of a data system that Trump officials overhauled. The system has erroneously flagged U.S. citizens and a lower court found it violated federal privacy protections.

entry.title: Is Switzerland's neutrality at a crossroads?
entry.summary: Switzerland is voting on whether to tighten its famous neutrality — a move that could reshape its response to Russia and future conflicts.

entry.title: The U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve is low. Here's why you should care
entry.summary: The U.S. has tapped into its strategic oil reserve to help drive down rising gasoline prices in the wake of the war with Iran. Can oil from Venezuela help fill it back up?

entry.title: How stores choose what to put on their shelves — like, say, Planet Money's board game
entry.summary: The most coveted real estate in business might just be the choicest shelf space of national big box retail. We go inside the room and the process of how stores choose what you can and can't buy.

entry.title: Foreign ministers of the Americas to discuss Nicaragua in meeting called by the U.S.
entry.summary: The U.S. is pushing the Americas to confront Nicaragua—but what, if anything, the region is prepared to do remains unclear.

entry.title: Demand for ambulance helicopters is going up, but it's hard to retain staff
entry.summary: Rural hospital closures are driving demand for air ambulance services. But finding and keeping highly trained staff to practice medicine in the air isn't easy.

entry.title: Here's what's on the docket for Pope Leo XIV's first papal visit to France since 2008
entry.summary: In the first papal state visit to France in nearly 20 years, Pope Leo will preside over Mass in Paris, meet with sex abuse survivors and deliver a speech on European unity.

entry.title: Thousands of people gather for a South African barbecue, aiming to set a world record
entry.summary: South Africa is aiming to smash a savory world record — the world's largest BBQ — and more boerewors sausage than you can shake a stick at.
